references.text: The parallel passage in Deuteronomy where the Ten Commandments are repeated, with the same prohibition against false testimony.
Elaborates on the prohibition against false testimony by warning against spreading false rumors and being a malicious witness.
Prohibition against lying and deceit toward one's neighbor, expanding on the principle of truthfulness in relationships with others.
Legislation concerning false witnesses and the consequences for those who testify falsely against their neighbor.
The book of Proverbs lists things the Lord hates, including a false witness who speaks lies.
The contrast between a truthful witness and a false witness who speaks lies.
Warns that a false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever speaks lies will not escape.
Repeats the warning that a false witness will not go unpunished.
Compares giving false testimony against one's neighbor to using a dangerous weapon.
Jesus cites this commandment as part of the commands one must keep to inherit eternal life.
Jesus mentions the prohibition against false testimony in his conversation with the rich young man.
Luke's version of Jesus' quotation of the commandment against false testimony.
Paul summarizes the commandments, including this one, under the command of love.
Expands the commandment from a legal prohibition to a matter of personal truthfulness and motivation.
Places lying and deceit as a form of theft against one's neighbor, expanding the understanding of its harmful effects.
Warns against group pressure as the primary reason why people break the commandment not to give false testimony.
